# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX Audit

**Evidence note.** This audit distinguishes documented behavior from design recommendations. Woslicer III’s complete shortcut/format specification, PTSEQUENCER’s authoritative manual, and accessible YouTube comments were not found in the fetched material; those fields are marked “not documented,” rather than inferred.

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow | Top 3 pain points / limits | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sayaslicer** | Load/drag audio → add/import markers (MIDI, BMSE clipboard, iBMSC) → snap/edit/preview → copy editor data and/or export keysounds → save project. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) | (1) Zero-crossing reduces clicks but moves markers and can break iBMSC timing; BMSE export rounds to 192th. [important notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) (2) Partial BPM changes are “a bit hackish”; better grid/clipboard BPM support is planned. [planned features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features) (3) Linux PipeWire preview crash, macOS quarantine friction, and >2GB-file failure were reported. [issues](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues) | No slice-count ceiling documented. Snap 1/1–1/192; iBMSC can exceed 192th, while BMSE rounds to nearest 192th. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) | Individual keysound export (`M`), keysound list/BMS append, BMSE or iBMSC clipboard, project save. [shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts) |
| **Woslicer II** | Load WAV → BPM/offset/grid → marker edits → preview → batch WAV output → paste clip/sequence into BMSE. [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | Many files make one-by-one BMSE definition “hard work”; output order depends on Explorer/drag order; unsupported/24/32-bit WAVs may fail or force-quit. [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer) | No numeric maximum documented. Grid defaults to 16ths and is adjustable; dedicated snap terminology not documented. [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | Numbered WAVs plus Woslicer clip/sequence data pasted into BMSE. [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) |
| **Woslicer III** | Drag WAV → set BPM/granularity → click markers (right-click removes) → `P`/Enter preview → wave output and optional `.wos` → paste sequence and define WAVs in BMSE. [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Tail/end adjustment is explicitly easy to overlook; guides warn about pop noise/clicks; WAV incompatibility can crash. [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer) | No numeric maximum or complete III shortcut list documented; grid granularity is selectable. [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Exported WAVs, `.wos` marker data, and clipboard sequence for BMSE. [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) |
| **BMHelper / Mid2BMS** | Export MIDI → analyze/split/reuse notes → render audio → import cut positions into Woslicer or use generated files → insert definitions/sequence into BMSE/iBMSC. [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html), [workflow](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) | MIDI/DAW round trip and tool switching; Mid2BMS requires folder/name conventions and manual TXT/BMS copying; deleted sounds may need manual restoration. [Mid2BMS tutorial](https://mid2bms.net/tutorial.html) | No universal max documented. BMHelper exposes minimum interval, sorting, similarity thresholds and multiple definitions; BMS base36 gives 1,296 two-character IDs, while base62 gives 3,843 in the cited reference. [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html), [BMS memo](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm), [keysound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | Generated WAV/renamer arrays, text/BMS definitions and clipboard sequence; Mid2BMS input is WAV-oriented and its reference says OGG is unsupported at that stage. [reference](https://mid2bms.net/reference.html) |
| **PTSEQUENCER** | No reliable fetched manual/workflow. | The requested exact limit is inconsistent across fetched secondary evidence: NamuWiki reports historical DJMAX tooling at 1,023 and DPC 2025 at 2,047, while saying excess loaded files can malfunction. Treat as a compatibility budget, not a guaranteed current limit. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | 1,023/2,047 reported by the cited secondary source; snap not documented. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | Not documented in fetched authoritative material. |
| **dtinth/sound-slicer** | `.txt` timing/spec + WAV → numbered WAV parts + BMS clipboard text; MIDI helper supports rhythmic or melodic modes. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | Rhythmic mode can make slight gaps and 1,000 notes become 1,000 slices; melodic mode requires render/re-import; neither supports BPM changes. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | No general max; no BPM-change support. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | Numbered WAVs and clipboard text for BMx Sequence Editor. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) |
| **FL Studio Fruity Slicer 2** | Load audio → beat/marker auto-slice or edit markers → map slices to pads/Piano Roll/MIDI; BPM/stretch and per-slice gain/pan/envelope/filter controls. [manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer%202.htm) | BPM detection must be corrected when wrong; fine edits require zoom/drag; high-quality Sinc interpolation is slow. [manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer%202.htm), [export](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/fformats_save_export.htm) | Divisions include 1/6, 1/4, 1/3 beat etc.; no maximum documented. [manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer%202.htm) | Primarily mapped notes/Piano Roll; FL can render marker-bearing WAVs or split mixer tracks. [export](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/fformats_save_export.htm) |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline (P1)
- **Two coordinate systems are disconnected.** Existing workflows align BPM/offset/grid, then switch to audio slicing and finally to an editor; Woslicer’s documented default is 16ths and adjustable grid, while Sayaslicer’s better BPM display/clipboard support remains planned. [Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Sayaslicer planned features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features) **Recommendation:** dual waveform + chart ruler, shared playhead, ms and beat/bar labels, and explicit BPM-change segments.
- **Boundary quality is a timing/audio tradeoff (P1).** Zero-crossing reduces clicks but shifts markers and can invalidate iBMSC placement; Woslicer guidance says tails need manual adjustment and another guide reports III beginning pops. [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes), [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) **Recommendation:** show original vs adjusted boundary, with non-destructive per-slice Zero-X and fade.

### Interface (P1)
- **Export ceremony and context switching (P0).** Real workflow requires BMHelper → DAW render → Woslicer clipboard import → WAV export → BMSE file definitions → clipboard sequence paste; defining many files one-by-one is explicitly hard work. [purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)
- **File ordering is a hidden dependency (P0).** BMSE definitions follow Explorer ordering and drag order, so users must preselect the start ID and keep names ordered. [purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
- **Dense shortcuts help power users but are discoverability debt (P2).** Woslicer II uses BPM, offset, grid, marker, preview and export hotkeys; Sayaslicer adds many marker/clipboard/project hotkeys. [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Sayaslicer shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts) **Recommendation:** command palette, visible shortcut hints, undo/redo, and keyboard-layout-aware bindings.
- **Onboarding/platform friction (P1).** Sayaslicer reports Linux preview crashes under PipeWire, unsigned macOS builds requiring quarantine removal, and large-file loading failures. [issue 12](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/12), [issue 8](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/8), [issue 5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5)

### Settings (P1)
- **Snap precision versus editor compatibility (P0).** Sayaslicer supports 1/1–1/192 and iBMSC beyond 192th, but zero-crossing can make iBMSC data fail; BMSE rounds to 192th. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features), [notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) **Recommendation:** Snap 1/4–1/192 plus free/ms mode, with a compatibility badge and automatic “round for target.”
- **Tail/reverb policy is implicit (P1).** BMHelper exposes minimum interval specifically when releases/reverb would interfere; community guidance says long pads/reverb/delay are often better BGM than keysounds to control size. [purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/4de2639ea97bc6723650) **Recommendation:** per-slice tail mode: preserve, fade, silence-threshold trim, or BGM-only.
- **Format/settings failures are poorly surfaced (P1).** Woslicer users are told to resave unsupported WAVs via SoundEngine/Audacity and check 24/32-bit; Mid2BMS documents WAV naming and an OGG restriction. [Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer), [reference](https://mid2bms.net/reference.html) **Recommendation:** preflight format/bit-depth/channel checks with actionable conversion, not a crash.

### Backend (P0)
- **Traditional export creates a fragile asset graph.** Numbered WAVs, definitions and sequence clipboard data must remain aligned; misordering and unused-file cleanup are recurring community concerns. [purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Wix](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make2), [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/4de2639ea97bc6723650)
- **Identifier/key-count budgets matter.** BMS base36 is 1,296 IDs and cited base62 is 3,843; secondary DJMAX evidence reports 1,023/2,047 historical PTSEQUENCER-era capacity and warns of excess-file malfunctions. [BMS memo](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm), [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A음) **Recommendation:** virtual slices should preserve one source asset, deduplicate/reuse, and show target budget before finalize.
- **Playback semantics differ by target (P1).** The reference says older same-track playback could interrupt the prior sample, while Technika 2 onward changed to non-interfering inputs; BMS can require over-definition to avoid same-ID retrigger behavior. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A음) **Recommendation:** BMS/RESPECT/TECHNIKA mode profiles must validate overlap, retrigger and voice behavior rather than silently export.
- **BPM handling is a known weak point (P1).** Sayaslicer calls partial BPM support hackish; sound-slicer has no BPM-change support; BMHelper/Woslicer rely on BPM/offset matching. [Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features), [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer — keep these

1. **Keep Woslicer’s fast keyboard loop and audible verification:** marker movement, preview, and advance are central to throughput. [Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)
2. **Keep direct BMSE clipboard interoperability**, because it removes manual definition/sequence placement. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
3. **Keep iBMSC export for >192th work, but expose target compatibility.** Sayaslicer explicitly supports this and documents the failure mode. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)
4. **Keep project save/load, marker copy/paste, undo/redo and keysound-list export**—these are the foundations of a resumable, non-destructive workflow. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
5. **Keep configurable silent-tail removal, fadeout, offset and zero-crossing**, but make each reversible/per-slice. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
6. **Keep cross-platform intent and localization**, while fixing the concrete macOS/Linux onboarding failures. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [issues](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues)

## 4. Top 10 recommendations, prioritized

1. **P0 — Make slicing non-destructive and first-class in the Studio project.** Store `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` and create notes immediately; export WAV/OGG only at finalize. This directly removes the numbered-file/definition/order failure documented in BMSE workflows. [purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Wix](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make2)
2. **P0 — Add “Import to Studio” and round-trip metadata.** Preserve source identity, bounds, target ID and note references so a finalized export can be edited back without re-slicing. Existing clipboard workflows are one-way/context-switch heavy. [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html), [Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
3. **P0 — Use a dual timeline.** Top: chart preview/notes; bottom: waveform; shared playhead, zoom, bar/beat/ms rulers and BPM-change lanes. This addresses the documented BPM/offset/grid ceremony and weak BPM-change support. [Woslicer](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features)
4. **P0 — Add target modes BMS / RESPECT / TECHNIKA with preflight.** Validate IDs, snap resolution, overlap/retrigger semantics, audio format and key-count budget; show warnings before export. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A8%EC%9D%8C), [BMS memo](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm)
5. **P1 — Implement robust Zero-X with reversible alternatives.** Offer Zero-X off/on, nearest crossing, fade-in/out and “preserve chart time”; visually show moved boundaries and flag iBMSC incompatibility. [Sayaslicer notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes), [issue #2](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/2)
6. **P1 — Make snap explicit and compatible.** Provide 1/4–1/192, free-ms, BPM-aware grid, resnap, and “round to target” preview. Sayaslicer proves both arbitrary snap and 192th compatibility are needed. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
7. **P1 — Add a Slice Library with reuse/deduplication and budget meter.** Search, audition, tag, duplicate-reference, and show unique slices vs note instances; this counters key-count/capacity pressure and supports phrase-aware authoring. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음)
8. **P1 — Add per-slice overrides.** Zero-X, fade, normalize, tail trim/preserve, gain and channel policy should be local overrides over project defaults; tail/reverb and format mismatches are currently manual. [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html), [Fruity Slicer manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer%202.htm)
9. **P1 — Add a command palette and visible keyboard map.** Preserve fast keys for experts, but make `Z`, `P`, preview/advance, snap, export and undo discoverable; Woslicer/Sayaslicer workflows are shortcut dense. [Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Sayaslicer shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts)
10. **P1 — Preflight, autosave and diagnostic export.** Detect unsupported WAV bit depth, channel/codec, long-file risk, missing source, duplicate IDs, unassigned notes and over-budget targets; autosave virtual-slice projects and export a human-readable mapping. [Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer), [Sayaslicer issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5), [iBMSC](https://github.com/aqtq314/iBMSC)

## 5. Proposed feature validation

**Dual timeline + mode switcher + Import to Studio is strongly validated by the evidence.** Existing tools split the work across audio, MIDI, clipboard, file export and BMSE; Woslicer requires BPM/offset/grid alignment and later file/sequence placement, while Sayaslicer still calls proper BPM-change grid/clipboard handling a planned feature. [Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Sayaslicer planned features](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features) The proposed virtual-slice model specifically removes the documented failure surface of filename order, hundreds of definitions, and manual one-by-one placement. [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)

**Keep the limitation explicit:** do not claim that one overlap rule fits all targets. The fetched reference distinguishes older interruptive playback from Technika 2+ non-interfering playback and reports changing key-count budgets; the mode switcher must encode those differences. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음)
